text.text: One home for the whole thesis: chapters and word counts, the reading queue, the weekly task list and notes from every advisor meeting. Update word counts every Friday.
Draft deadlines per chapter are on the Chapters calendar. Move a deadline when the advisor agrees a new plan.
Words now against the word target gives a rough picture only. Revision removes words as often as it adds them; judge by structure first.
Target about 600 new words on a writing day. Progress is words now divided by the word target.
Draft progress compares words now with the word target.
Draft status flags chapters past or near their draft date.
A chapter in review with open tasks needs those tasks closed before the date.
Start this list eight weeks before the date. Each item is small; the list prevents surprises.
Full draft sent to committee four weeks ahead
References checked against the style guide
Practise answers to three hard questions
Week 8: slides outline and a three-minute summary of the contribution.
Week 4: full talk to a friendly audience; record it.
Week 1: mock questions from two colleagues, then rest.
A line a day is enough. Note what you wrote, how long it took and what comes next.
After each session record the date, the words written and what stopped you. Look back monthly for a pattern: time of day, location, or task type that works.
